title: SSE partial-frame provenance and deterministic reassembly for toolcall preemption
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight per-chunk provenance header and deterministic reassembly rules for SSE streams so clients can safely reconnect, resume, and handle mid-stream tool/function call preemption without corrupting structured outputs. This ticket scopes the server-side protocol changes, backward-compatible client handshake fields, and a migration/fallback mode for legacy consumers. The goal is resilience: when a client disconnects mid-frame or mid-toolcall, it can reconnect and request only the missing semantic suffix or request a compact diff, and the server can prove chunk ownership and position without storing the entire transcript for long periods.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a provenance token per logical chunk (base64-encoded HMAC) and a sequence index; tokens are verifiable by the server for +/- 5s window.
Reconnect handshake allows client to send last-seen-provenance and desired resume mode: suffix-only | diff | resync-full.

Tool/function-call boundaries are marked with an explicit 'call-boundary' flag in chunk metadata, and preempted calls produce a stable 'call-token' which can be used to request replay of tool output only.
Clients using legacy handshake get a backward-compatible stream (no provenance) and receive a clear deprecation header; no legacy client should break.

End-to-end tests demonstrate recovery for these scenarios: (a) disconnect inside JSON-structured output, (b) disconnect after function-call invocation before tool response, (c) reconnect with suffix-only request and successful merge without duplicate tool invocations.
Performance regression <= 3% p50 latency overhead under typical small-chunk workloads compared to current SSE baseline.
Security review sign-off for HMAC key handling and provenance token entropy.
Docs PR and SDK shim added to the JS and Python clients with sample reconnect code.
implementation_notes: Provenance token format: base64(HMAC_SHA256(secret_key, sequence_index || chunk_hash || timestamp_ms)) with TTL embedded in timestamp_ms.
Chunk metadata fields over SSE comment lines: seq=<int>;prov=<token>;flags=call-boundary|final-piece|partial-json|legacy

Server keeps an in-memory ring journal of chunk headers and compact hashes for last 60s or last N chunks (configurable per-tenant). Full bodies are not retained; only enough to answer suffix-only replay requests where the suffix fits within journal window.
If client requests 'diff' resume mode, server computes a compact patch using chunk hashes and returns only delta frames; fallback to resync-full if patch exceeds size threshold.

Toolcall preemption: when a function call is detected mid-stream, server emits a call-token and marks following chunks until tool response with call-token. On reconnect, client can request 'replay-tool-output' with call-token; server ensures single-at-most tool invocation by consulting the call-invocation ledger.
Backpressure: provenance headers incur ~64 bytes per chunk; prefer adaptive chunk sizing to amortize header overhead. Add advisor in Optimize to suggest chunk_size per workload.

Compatibility: Introduce Accept-Streaming-Provenance header for clients to opt-in. Default for existing clients is legacy mode for 90 days post-rollout, then opt-out enforced with deprecation schedule.
Telemetry: emit traces for resume attempts, provenance verification failures, and repeated partial reconnects per session.
Feature-flag the journaling window and provenance TTL per customer to allow conservative rollout for enterprise tenants.
Edge-proxy behavior: proxies must forward SSE comment lines intact; provide Nginx/LB config snippet in docs.
KMS: HMAC secret rotated via KMS with online key id in header; include key-id in provenance token to allow server verification after rotation.
Failure modes: if provenance verification fails on reconnect, server responds with resume_status=reject and optional guidance to resync-full.

Graceful degradation: for very long-running streams (>1h) where journal cannot cover full history, provide snapshot checkpoints at logical boundaries to allow suffix-only resumes tied to checkpoint ids.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable Accept-Streaming-Provenance on internal staging and 3% of traffic; keep default legacy mode.
Phase 2 (tenant opt-in): provide console toggle for customers to opt into provenanced streams; monitor errors and performance for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (wider rollout): enable provenance for all new sessions; send deprecation notices to legacy clients; keep journal and replay endpoints behind feature-flag for 60 days.
Phase 4 (enforced): after 90 days and client SDK updates, flip default to provenance and remove legacy-only code paths incrementally.
Emergency rollback: feature flag off and immediate deprecation header removal; fall back to current SSE emission without provenance tokens.
qa_tests: Unit: token generation and verification with rotated keys and expired TTLs.
Integration: simulated client disconnects at byte offsets inside JSON fragments; reconnect with suffix-only; assert merged JSON validity and no duplicate function invocations.
Chaos: random mid-stream TCP drops under high concurrency; measure resume success rate and memory usage.
Compatibility: legacy client handshake and modern client handshake coexistence tests behind proxies (NGINX and ALB).
Load: 5k concurrent streaming sessions with provenance enabled to validate <3% latency overhead and journal memory bounds.
